definition: Generating intelligible speech audio from silent lip movements — bridging lipreading and TTS for silent speech interfaces.
details: Generating intelligible speech audio from silent lip movements — bridging lipreading and TTS for silent speech interfaces.

explainer.lead: Lip to speech synthesis generates intelligible speech audio from silent lip movements. It matters for silent speech interfaces, connecting lipreading with text-to-speech so speech can be recovered without audible input.

tiers.eli5: It watches a person's silent mouth movements and turns them into spoken words you can hear.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers pair a visual front end that reads lip movements with a speech generation stage to produce audio. The pitfall is that visual cues are ambiguous, so output intelligibility depends heavily on the visual model.
tiers.paperLevel: The task is generating intelligible speech audio from silent lip movements, bridging lipreading and text-to-speech for silent speech interfaces. The definition sets no standard for intelligibility or for the visual-to-audio architecture used.

explainer.example: A silent speech interface records a speaker mouthing a phrase with no audio and outputs synthesized speech of that phrase.
